decisions.source_zh_cn: 代理理事长团队战　长距离代表
decisions.note: Pinned repository evidence only identifies this as a race_name/internal team-race representative label and does not establish a stable canonical race name; defer rather than normalize from zh-CN.
JRA/Horse Racing in Japan uses the official English race name Queen Elizabeth II Cup; the zh-CN source identifies the same established race.

decisions.source_zh_cn: 优骏牝马（日本橡树大赛）
decisions.note: JRA/Horse Racing in Japan uses Yushun Himba (Japanese Oaks); preserve that established race name rather than calquing zh-CN.
Horse Racing in Japan race schedules use Shinetsu Stakes for this established JRA race.

ja: ルミエールオータムダッシュ
decisions.note: Horse Racing in Japan schedules use Lumiere Autumn Dash; use the established proper race name, with zh-CN only as the semantic bridge.
Horse Racing in Japan's NAR schedule uses Zen-Nippon Nisai Yushun for the established Kawasaki dirt race.
Current Horse Racing in Japan schedules use Rokko Stakes.
JRA uses Kyodo News Hai (Tokinominoru Kinen); the assigned base label 共同通信杯 is canonically represented as Kyodo News Hai.
Horse Racing in Japan's current NAR principal-race schedule uses Kanto Oaks.
JRA/Horse Racing in Japan graded-race schedules use Sekiya Kinen.
Horse Racing in Japan race schedules use Kanetsu Stakes.

ja: チャンピオンズカップ
decisions.note: JRA/Horse Racing in Japan uses Champions Cup as the official English G1 race name.
JRA materials use Phoenix Sho for the established race; retain the proper-name romanization rather than translating 凤凰 literally.
Current Horse Racing in Japan schedules use Hosu Stakes.
JRA/Horse Racing in Japan uses the established international name Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.
Current JRA/Horse Racing in Japan graded-race materials use Hakodate Nisai Stakes.

ja: 函館スプリントステークス
decisions.note: Current JRA/Horse Racing in Japan schedules use Hakodate Sprint Stakes.
Current JRA/Horse Racing in Japan graded-race materials use Hakodate Kinen.
JRA materials use Hiiragi Sho; preserve the established race name instead of translating the zh-CN plant term literally.
Current Horse Racing in Japan schedules use Wasurenagusa Sho.
